description: We are making something visually engaging
summary:
Space Legacy: Abandoned, But Not Lost is an interactive web museum and 3D exploration playground showcasing thirteen historic NASA spacecraft, rovers, and lunar stations resting across the Moon, Mars, and interstellar space. We developed visual scroll-animated storyboards, a live Three.js 3D hardware playground with an “Unmerge” feature that floats major components apart with child-friendly explanations, a heliocentric AU radar, authentic NASA audio feeds, read-aloud narration, an AI Cosmic Dictionary, and encrypted explorer accounts.
Rather than treating dormant spacecraft as forgotten junk, our platform answers NASA’s “Abandoned, But Not Lost” storytelling challenge by transforming dense telemetry logs into self-explanatory visual journeys built for ten-year-old learners—celebrating how each machine worked, its final signal, and the discoveries left behind.
This matters because preserving off-world engineering heritage makes STEM accessible worldwide, turning silent monuments billions of miles away into living classrooms that ignite curiosity and inspire humanity’s next generation of scientists and space explorers.
details:
What Our Project Does & How It Works

Space Legacy: Abandoned, But Not Lost is an interactive digital museum, 3D mechanical explorer, and story-driven science platform showcasing 13 historic NASA missions currently resting on the Moon, parked on Mars, or cruising through deep space—spanning Apollo Lunar Hardware, ALSEP Stations, Pioneer 10 & 11, Voyager 1 & 2, Cassini, New Horizons, LRO, and Mars explorers Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, Curiosity, InSight, and Perseverance & Ingenuity.

Instead of leaving retired spacecraft buried inside dense engineering archives, the web app invites curious learners—especially kids ages 10+—through five connected experiences:

  1. Home & Authentic Deep Space Audio Header: Visitors stream real NASA recordings (Apollo 11 Moon comms, Voyager's Golden Record, and Perseverance's Martian wind) and solve the Daily Signal Mystery to decode Opportunity’s final transmission.
  2. Illustrated 6-Chapter Scroll Stories (Catalogue): Every mission opens an interactive visual story pairing plain-English storytelling, custom animated diagrams, authentic NASA photography, one-click audio narration, and three selectable reading depths (Junior Explorer, Space Cadet, Mission Scientist).
  3. Interactive 3D "Unmerge" Playground: Built with Three.js WebGL, users rotate all 13 spacecraft in 360° and click Unmerge to smoothly separate each machine mid-air into 5 major components with floating labels and kid-friendly explanations when tapped.
  4. Heliocentric AU Telemetry Radar: Maps all 13 spacecraft live from lunar distance (0.0026 AU) out into interstellar space (162+ AU).
  5. Confidential Explorer Accounts & Universal Cosmic Dictionary: Clicking any highlighted space term opens an instant everyday analogy powered by Google Gemini (with a built-in offline glossary fallback), while quizzes and badges are verified server-side inside isolated, encrypted user accounts.

Benefits

  • Zero-Jargon Understanding: Turns complex terms (RTG, seismometer, Kapton foil, delta-V) into relatable everyday comparisons within seconds.
  • Built for Every Learning Style: Blends interactive 3D disassembly, visual motion storytelling, authentic NASA soundscapes, and full read-aloud voice narration.
  • Reliable & Private: Works smoothly even without an API key or stable connection via offline fallbacks, and strictly isolates every user's streaks, badges, and progress from other accounts.

Intended Impact

Our mission is to replace the idea of "abandoned space junk" with lasting STEM wonder—helping children and families see that every silent lander, orbiter, and rover is a monument to human curiosity that exceeded its mission. By turning technical archives into an inviting hands-on playground, the platform empowers students everywhere to understand how space engineering works and imagine themselves building what comes next.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • AI Design & Development Platforms: Google Stitch AI (UI/UX layout ideation and visual prototyping), Google AI Studio (full-stack prototyping, architecture iteration, and interactive prompt engineering), and Google Gemini (@google/genai / gemini-3-flash-preview) (code assistance, kid-friendly editorial synthesis, and live Cosmic Dictionary word explanations)
  • Languages: TypeScript (^7.0.2), HTML5, CSS3 (Tailwind CSS v4), JavaScript (ESM)
  • Frontend & 3D Graphics: React 19 (react, react-dom), Vite (^8.3.0), Tailwind CSS (@tailwindcss/vite), Three.js (three procedural PBR materials, OrbitControls, raycasting), Lucide React (lucide-react)
  • Backend, Cryptography & Audio: Node.js (>=20), Express.js (express), tsx, dotenv, Node crypto (scryptSync, AES-256-GCM, SHA-256 tokens, rate limiting), Web Crypto / Web Audio APIs, Google Translate TTS proxy (/api/tts), and Browser Web Speech Synthesis

How the Project Is Creative

  • Mechanical Storytelling in 3D: Rather than static photos or overly complex CAD files, pressing Unmerge smoothly floats 5 key subsystems of each of the 13 spacecraft apart mid-air so young explorers can tap any part and instantly learn what it does.
  • Tap-Any-Word Curiosity: Readers never get stuck on unfamiliar vocabulary—every tricky term connects directly to a live pronunciation guide and kid analogy without leaving the story.
  • Visual-First Story Chapters: Abstract physics and engineering events (like Apollo’s two-stage liftoff using its golden lower half as a Moon launchpad, or Spirit digging pure silica with a jammed wheel) are rebuilt as intuitive animated scenes even a 10-year-old understands at first glance.

Engineering Factors Considered (Energy, Accessibility, Cost, & Privacy)

  • Energy & Compute Efficiency: All 13 interactive 3D spacecraft are generated procedurally in Three.js without heavy multi-megabyte model downloads; mission photography is lazy-loaded (loading="lazy"); Gemini dictionary responses are cached server-side to prevent redundant AI requests; and the 3D render loop paces itself cleanly on low-power devices.
  • Accessibility (a11y): Uses semantic <button> controls, keyboard navigation, Escape-key modal dismissal, high-contrast typography, three reading tracks, and full read-aloud audio narration across all 13 missions.
  • Cost & Offline Resilience: Uses zero paid database infrastructure and automatically falls back to a curated local dictionary and native browser speech synthesis if an API key is absent or offline.
  • Account Privacy & Integrity: User accounts use unique scrypt-salted passcodes, per-account AES-256-GCM encrypted vaults, tab-scoped session tokens cleared completely on sign-out, and server-side verification for quiz and mystery rewards.

AI Disclosure, Watermarking, Metadata & NASA Branding Compliance

  • How Google Stitch AI, Google AI Studio & Google Gemini Were Used:
    • UI Ideation & Code: Google Stitch AI was used to explore and structure early interface layouts, and Google AI Studio powered by Google Gemini was used to assist in writing and refining the React/TypeScript frontend, Three.js procedural spacecraft geometry, Express backend APIs, and educational summaries.
    • Data / Dynamic Content: Google Gemini (gemini-3-flash-preview) powers optional live Universal Cosmic Dictionary explanations (generating kid-friendly analogies and space facts with local dictionary fallback when offline).
    • Audio: Mission story chapter narrations (/public/audio/*-1.mp3 to *-6.mp3) and /api/tts playback were generated using AI text-to-speech (Google Translate TTS / Web Speech synthesis), distinct from authentic archival NASA audio clips (apollo-11-eagle.mp3, voyager-golden-record.mp3, mars-perseverance-wind.mp3).
    • All mission photographs displayed inside /public/images/missions/ and /public/images/sectors/ are unaltered, authentic public-domain NASA archival photographs (not AI-generated images).
    • The custom application emblem (/public/images/space-legacy-logo.svg), UI graphics, and Three.js 3D models are original non-NASA designs. No content generated with Google Stitch AI, Google AI Studio, or Google Gemini uses, contains, replicates, or modifies any official NASA logos, insignia, or NASA branding/design elements.
